sg.ra: Choose Rows D-L for a comfortable distance that retains stage detail. Center seats have a direct angle to the stage. Rows H-L are under the Mezzanine overhang, which can cut off the top of the stage.

Choose Rows A-C for excellent elevated views, with a clear view of the full performance from a comfortable distance. Expect to pay the highest prices in the Center Mezzanine for these front rows. Prefer Row A if avoiding the Balcony overhang matters, because it starts at Row B.
Rows D-E provide a clean, direct view of the stage. Expect a possible minor obstruction at the top of the stage because the Balcony overhang begins at Row B.

Choose rows A or B in the Center Balcony for the best overhead views in this section. They give a clear, complete view but are distant, so fine details are less clear. These seats are especially effective for musicals with ensemble choreography.

Avoid the last few Balcony rows if you can because the view is not great and sound issues have been reported. Seats behind the pillars between rows B and C can have bisected sightlines, although you may be able to lean around them. If you must sit here, choose an aisle seat for more legroom.

sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang kicks in at row H, and seats behind this may experience cut-off at the top of the stage.
sn.sh: Mezzanine overhang kicks in at row H

sn.lo: Center Orchestra, rows AA to B
sn.c: Rows AA, A and B can be too close because the angle leads to neck craning.
sn.sh: Rows AA to B can be too close

sn.c: Towards the far sides in the Left and Right Mezzanine, views tend to become more obstructed by the Boxes and the angle towards the stage.
sn.sh: Far side views tend to be more obstructed

sn.lo: Center Balcony, rows B to C
sn.c: Four thin pillars are located between rows B and C at the edge of the Center Balcony.
sn.sh: Thin pillars between rows B and C

sn.c: The middle rows in the Center Mezzanine are a good value option for elevated sightlines that don’t feel distant.
sn.sh: Elevated sightlines that don’t feel distant

sn.lo: Center Balcony, rows A to B
sn.c: Rows A and B of the Center Balcony are the best views in this high and more distant section.
sn.sh: Best views in the Balcony section

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
